newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore noon stocks down, led by property selloff.
newsitem.headline: Singapore noon stocks down, led by property selloff.

text.p: Singapore shares weakened on Tuesday morning, led by heavy selling in property counters on persistent rumours of new government curbs on the sector, dealers said.

"There are these talks the government will be announcing new measures on the property market this weekend and that is causing a lot of nervousness across the board," said a broker at a local house. He said selling by foreign institutions further dampened sentiment.
Singapore has seen two sets of curbs so far. The first was in May last year, followed by a second on April 12.
The Straits Times Industrials Index shed 14.71 points to hit a 27-month low at 1,982.08.

The SES property index hit a new low at 640.35 before inching to 643.19, down 13.85 points, or 2.11 percent. The index was led down by property heavyweights City Developments and Wing Tai Holdings, which fell 50 cents and 22 cents respectively to hit new year lows of S$11.50 and S$3.62.

Foreign tranches of banks like UOB and DBS were also hit by the bearish sentiment. "It's difficult to say if the market has hit its bottom. But long term investors could find value stocks at this stage," another broker said. -- Angela Tan (65 8703083)
